claims.text: Current-dollar PCE increased $32.7 billion in May 2022; real goods decreased 1.6 percent while real services increased 0.3 percent, so both did NOT decrease.

citations.quotation: Disposable personal income (DPI) increased $96.5 billion (0.5 percent) and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $32.7 billion (0.2 percent).
Real DPI decreased 0.1 percent in May and Real PCE decreased 0.4 percent; goods decreased 1.6 percent and services increased 0.3 percent (tables 5 and 7).

counterarguments.text: A possible confusion: in current dollars, goods spending decreased ($43.5 billion) while services increased ($76.2 billion), which might be misread as real changes; the real percentage changes are stated separately.

citations.quotation: The $32.7 billion increase in current-dollar PCE in May reflected an increase of $76.2 billion in spending for services that was partly offset by a decrease of $43.5 billion in spending for goods (table 3).

limitations: The sources are partial excerpts of the BEA release; underlying tables 5 and 7 values are not shown directly.
The release is the June 30, 2022 publication covering May 2022 data; the dates are declared by the source and not independently verified.

citation.quotation: personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $32.7 billion (0.2 percent).
